For teachers and tutors

Practise the basics.
Keep the evidence visible.

Use automatic training for a balanced short session, or choose a specific exercise from the Year 1–6 syllabus. The report separates recent independent accuracy from later-day match-fit evidence.

Open the academy

Useful ways to use the resource

Brief independent practice

Use a short session after an idea has been taught. Coach combines weaknesses, fact recall and a wider year-map sample.

Targeted follow-up

Select a table, column level or named curriculum family. Mathematical hints remain supported evidence rather than independent success.

Practical observation

Record explanation, measuring, constructions and model-making in the practical checklist. A virtual tool does not establish correct use of a real one.

Understand the limits of the evidence

The warm-up samples a starting point; it is not a diagnostic test. Response time includes reading and input. The programme’s thresholds are transparent product rules, not externally validated attainment measures. A local leaderboard encourages shared-device play but is not an authenticated assessment or online class service.

Detailed history keeps recent matches, while lifetime XP, personal records and recall data are retained separately. Export CSV results for a selected learner, and use JSON backup/restore to move a squad between browsers.
